lead: No natural product has strong evidence in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS). The best-studied, coenzyme Q10 combined with NADH, has three randomized trials from one research group that reported less fatigue, but a 2025 systematic review rated the supplement studies at high risk of bias (grade B). A 6-month placebo-controlled trial of vitamin D found no effect on fatigue (grade: Negative).

grade_key.A: Meta-analysis, or at least 2 randomized trials with low risk of bias and a consistent benefit
grade_key.B: 1 good randomized trial, or several randomized trials with mixed results
grade_key.C: Observational studies, small pilots or open-label trials only
grade_key.Negative: Randomized trials found no benefit over placebo

disclaimer: This page summarizes published research. It is not medical advice. Talk to a clinician before starting any supplement, especially if you take other medicines.

products.name: Coenzyme Q10 plus NADH
products.summary: Three placebo-controlled trials come from one research group; the first two share one trial registration. In an 8-week trial in 73 people, 200 mg of CoQ10 with 20 mg of NADH a day reduced fatigue impact scores more than placebo. An 8-week trial in 80 people found lower fatigue than with placebo; maximum heart rate on exercise testing fell from baseline within the supplement group, and pain and sleep did not change. A 12-week trial in 207 people reported improvements in cognitive fatigue and quality of life within the supplement group compared with its own starting point. A 2025 systematic review found the supplement studies in ME/CFS had a high risk of bias, and a 2020 review of 55 randomized ME/CFS trials listed CoQ10 plus NADH among 8 interventions with statistically significant results but found no treatment with consistent, reproducible benefit.
products.safety_interactions: The 80-person trial reported the combination was generally safe and well tolerated. Across 14 supplement studies in ME/CFS, the systematic review found six that noted adverse effects, including nausea and insomnia. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Coenzyme Q10
general_safety.short: Few adverse events were reported in trials. A case report describes reduced warfarin response while taking CoQ10.

general_safety.name: NADH
general_safety.short: A systematic review of 10 trials found NADH and NAD+ precursors well tolerated; reported effects included muscle pain, fatigue, sleep problems and headache.

products.name: Essential fatty acids (omega-3 and omega-6)
products.summary: Two 3-month placebo-controlled trials tested a capsule combining omega-6 (linoleic and gamma-linolenic acid) and omega-3 (EPA and DHA) fatty acids, with opposite results. A 1990 trial in 63 adults with postviral fatigue syndrome reported that 85% on the fatty acids and 17% on placebo felt improved at 3 months. A 1999 trial in 50 people, designed to repeat it using later diagnostic criteria for chronic fatigue syndrome, found no difference between the fatty acids and placebo. No trials of omega-3 on its own in ME/CFS were found in a PubMed search on 23 November 2026.
products.safety_interactions: The 1990 trial reported no adverse events. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Omega-3 fatty acids
general_safety.short: Linked to a higher risk of atrial fibrillation in cardiovascular trials, more so above 1 g/day; diarrhoea and altered taste were more likely than with placebo; bleeding findings are mixed.

citations.label: Behan et al., 1990, Acta Neurol Scand
citations.title: Effect of high doses of essential fatty acids on the postviral fatigue syndrome.

citations.label: Warren et al., 1999, Acta Neurol Scand
citations.title: The role of essential fatty acids in chronic fatigue syndrome. A case-controlled study of red-cell membrane essential fatty acids (EFA) and a placebo-controlled treatment study with high dose of EFA.

products.name: Melatonin with zinc
products.summary: In a 16-week double-blind randomized trial in 50 people with ME/CFS, melatonin (1 mg) with zinc (10 mg) once daily was compared with placebo. Physical fatigue was lower than with placebo at the final treatment visit, and the physical health summary score improved at every visit in the supplement group.
products.safety_interactions: The authors described the supplement as safe over 16 weeks. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trial.

general_safety.name: Melatonin
general_safety.short: Trial adverse events were few and mostly mild (daytime sleepiness, headache, dizziness); long-term data are limited. Drugs acting on CYP1A2 may slow its breakdown.

general_safety.name: Zinc
general_safety.short: Nausea and bad taste were more common with zinc in common-cold trials. Case reports link zinc supplements and zinc overload to copper deficiency, causing anaemia or nerve damage.

citations.label: Castro-Marrero et al., 2021, Antioxidants (Basel)
citations.title: Effect of Melatonin Plus Zinc Supplementation on Fatigue Perception in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.

products.name: NADH on its own
products.summary: Two placebo-controlled trials have mixed results. In a crossover trial in 26 people, 10 mg of NADH a day for 4 weeks was compared with placebo; 8 of 26 responded favorably to NADH against 2 of 26 to placebo. A larger 3-month trial, in which NADH or placebo was given for the first 2 months and 77 of 86 people completed it, found no difference in most outcomes and no difference in how patients or investigators rated its effect, although anxiety and maximum heart rate after exercise testing fell with NADH.
products.safety_interactions: The crossover trial observed no severe adverse effects related to NADH. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: NADH
general_safety.short: A systematic review of 10 trials found NADH and NAD+ precursors well tolerated; reported effects included muscle pain, fatigue, sleep problems and headache.

citations.label: Forsyth et al., 1999, Ann Allergy Asthma Immunol
citations.title: Therapeutic effects of oral NADH on the symptoms of patients with chronic fatigue syndrome.

citations.label: Alegre et al., 2010, Rev Clin Esp
citations.title: [Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH) in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome].

products.name: Beta-glucan with vitamins and zinc
products.summary: In a 36-week double-blind randomized trial in 65 people with ME/CFS, yeast beta-glucan combined with vitamin D3, vitamin B6 and zinc was compared with placebo. Cognitive fatigue improved compared with the supplement group's own starting point; the abstract does not report a difference from placebo.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Beta-glucan
general_safety.short: Trials report mainly gastrointestinal symptoms, most frequent at the highest tablet dose; no major adverse events in a trial of an oat beta-glucan drink.

general_safety.name: Zinc
general_safety.short: Nausea and bad taste were more common with zinc in common-cold trials. Case reports link zinc supplements and zinc overload to copper deficiency, causing anaemia or nerve damage.

citations.label: Lacasa et al., 2023, Nutrients
citations.title: Yeast Beta-Glucan Supplementation with Multivitamins Attenuates Cognitive Impairments in Individuals with Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.

products.name: Coenzyme Q10 on its own (ubiquinol)
products.summary: A 12-week double-blind randomized trial of ubiquinol-10 against placebo enrolled 43 people with chronic fatigue syndrome, and 31 completed it. The abstract states only that it improved several symptoms, without giving figures, so the size of any effect cannot be judged from the abstract.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Coenzyme Q10
general_safety.short: Few adverse events were reported in trials. A case report describes reduced warfarin response while taking CoQ10.

citations.label: Fukuda et al., 2016, Biofactors
citations.title: Ubiquinol-10 supplementation improves autonomic nervous function and cognitive function in chronic fatigue syndrome.

products.name: D-ribose
products.summary: The only study is an uncontrolled, open-label pilot in 41 people with fibromyalgia and/or chronic fatigue syndrome, with no placebo group. Participants reported better energy, sleep, mental clarity, pain and well-being after taking D-ribose. No randomized trials of D-ribose in ME/CFS were found in a PubMed search on 23 November 2026.
products.safety_interactions: The pilot study reported D-ribose was well tolerated. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited study.

general_safety.name: D-ribose
general_safety.short: Human safety data are limited: an EFSA panel judged it safe up to 36 mg/kg body weight per day, and it was well tolerated in a small uncontrolled pilot study.

citations.label: Teitelbaum et al., 2006, J Altern Complement Med
citations.title: The use of D-ribose in chronic fatigue syndrome and fibromyalgia: a pilot study.

products.name: L-carnitine and acetyl-L-carnitine
products.summary: Neither trial used a placebo. An open-label 24-week trial randomized 90 people to acetyl-L-carnitine, propionyl-L-carnitine or both; mental fatigue improved with acetyl-L-carnitine and general fatigue with propionyl-L-carnitine, and 37% to 52% across the groups reported worse fatigue 2 weeks after stopping. A crossover trial in 30 people compared L-carnitine with the drug amantadine and reported improvement in 12 of 18 measures with L-carnitine.
products.safety_interactions: In the crossover trial, one person stopped L-carnitine because of diarrhea. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: L-carnitine and acetyl-L-carnitine
general_safety.short: In neuropathy trials, adverse events with acetyl-L-carnitine were similar to placebo; L-carnitine taken for 12 to 24 weeks raised blood TMAO, a compound linked to atherosclerosis.

citations.label: Vermeulen et al., 2004, Psychosom Med
citations.title: Exploratory open label, randomized study of acetyl- and propionylcarnitine in chronic fatigue syndrome.

citations.label: Plioplys et al., 1997, Neuropsychobiology
citations.title: Amantadine and L-carnitine treatment of Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.

products.name: Magnesium
products.summary: The only placebo-controlled trial, from 1991, gave magnesium sulphate by intramuscular injection, not by mouth. In 32 people over 6 weeks, 12 of 15 on magnesium and 3 of 17 on placebo said they felt better. No randomized trials of oral magnesium supplements in ME/CFS were found in a PubMed search on 23 November 2026.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Magnesium
general_safety.short: Oral magnesium mainly causes gastrointestinal effects such as diarrhoea; severe high blood magnesium occurs almost only in people with substantially reduced kidney function.

citations.label: Cox et al., 1991, Lancet
citations.title: Red blood cell magnesium and chronic fatigue syndrome.

products.name: Oxaloacetate
products.summary: In an open-label, non-randomized 6-week study, 76 people with ME/CFS took one of three doses of oxaloacetate; there was no concurrent placebo group, and results were compared with placebo results from an earlier, separate trial. Fatigue scores fell from baseline by 22.5% to 27.9%.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Oxaloacetate
general_safety.short: Small trials of 1 to 3 months in Alzheimer's disease and ME/CFS found oxaloacetate safe and well tolerated at the doses tested.

citations.label: Cash et al., 2022, J Transl Med
citations.title: Oxaloacetate Treatment For Mental And Physical Fatigue In Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) and Long-COVID fatigue patients: a non-randomized controlled clinical trial.

products.name: Probiotics
products.summary: Small placebo-controlled trials have mostly measured outcomes other than fatigue. In a 2-month pilot trial in 39 people, a Lactobacillus casei probiotic reduced anxiety scores. In a trial including 48 people with chronic fatigue syndrome, a Bifidobacterium infantis probiotic lowered blood markers of inflammation. In a 3-month trial in 26 people with ME/CFS after COVID-19, general fatigue fell in both the synbiotic and placebo groups, while post-exercise malaise improved more with the synbiotic. A 2018 systematic review judged the evidence for probiotics in ME/CFS poor and insufficient.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Probiotics
general_safety.short: Trials have not shown increased risk, though safety reporting is weak. Rare bloodstream infections occur, mainly in people who are severely ill, immunosuppressed or in intensive care.

products.name: Multivitamin and mineral supplements
products.summary: In a 10-week randomized trial in 53 people with chronic fatigue syndrome, a supplement containing several vitamins, minerals and coenzymes was compared with placebo. There were no differences in fatigue, symptom count or daily functioning, and no patient reported full recovery. An older crossover trial in 15 people tested injections of a liver extract containing folic acid and vitamin B12 and found no difference from placebo.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Multivitamin and mineral supplements
general_safety.short: COSMOS found no safety concerns or change in all-cause mortality with a daily multivitamin; Physicians' Health Study II found no change in cancer deaths.

citations.label: Brouwers et al., 2002, QJM
citations.title: The effect of a polynutrient supplement on fatigue and physical activity of patients with chronic fatigue syndrome: a double-blind randomized controlled trial.

citations.label: Kaslow et al., 1989, Arch Intern Med
citations.title: Liver extract-folic acid-cyanocobalamin vs placebo for chronic fatigue syndrome.

products.name: Vitamin D
products.summary: In a 6-month randomized trial in 50 people with chronic fatigue syndrome, 100,000 units of vitamin D3 every 2 months was compared with placebo. Vitamin D levels rose, but fatigue scores and markers of blood-vessel health did not improve.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Vitamin D
general_safety.short: Long-term supplementation raised the risk of high blood calcium and high urine calcium in trials, but not kidney stones; toxicity from extremely high doses is rare but serious.

citations.label: Witham et al., 2015, Nutr Metab Cardiovasc Dis
citations.title: Effect of intermittent vitamin D3 on vascular function and symptoms in chronic fatigue syndrome--a randomised controlled trial.
